successCriteria.description: IPolicyService interface declared in src/modules/policy/policy.service.interface.ts exporting getPolicyByLeaveType(leaveType: LeaveType): Promise<LeavePolicy[]>, getPolicyById(id: string): Promise<LeavePolicy | null>, getAllActivePolicies(): Promise<LeavePolicy[]>, createPolicy(policy: Omit<LeavePolicy, 'id' | 'createdAt' | 'updatedAt'>): Promise<LeavePolicy>, updatePolicy(id: string, policy: Partial<Omit<LeavePolicy, 'id' | 'createdAt' | 'updatedAt'>>): Promise<LeavePolicy | null>, deactivatePolicy(id: string): Promise<LeavePolicy | null>

PolicyService class in src/modules/policy/policy.service.ts implements IPolicyService, injects ILeavePolicyRepository via constructor, and delegates each method to the corresponding repository method: getPolicyByLeaveType → findByLeaveType, getPolicyById → findById, getAllActivePolicies → findAll({ isActive: true }), createPolicy → create, updatePolicy → update, deactivatePolicy → update(id, { isActive: false })

Jest unit tests in tests/unit/modules/policy/policy.service.test.ts covering all six IPolicyService methods: getPolicyByLeaveType returns policies for a valid LeaveType, getPolicyById returns policy when found and null when not found, getAllActivePolicies calls findAll with { isActive: true }, createPolicy delegates to repository create and returns the created policy, updatePolicy delegates to repository update and returns updated policy or null, deactivatePolicy calls update with { isActive: false } and returns the updated policy or null

constraints: Service must inject ILeavePolicyRepository via constructor — no direct DB access (GP-001)
PolicyService must implement IPolicyService exactly — all six methods with matching signatures
No imports from other modules' internals — policy is a leaf module; only import from policy.model.ts, policy.repository.ts, and shared/types/leave.types.ts
Tests must mock ILeavePolicyRepository and verify delegation, not database behavior
Strict TypeScript — no `any`, strict null checks, proper return types

ambiguities.description: deactivatePolicy implementation choice: repository has both update(id, { isActive: false }) returning LeavePolicy | null and softDelete(id) returning boolean. The intent specifies deactivatePolicy returns Promise<LeavePolicy | null>, favoring update over softDelete. If softDelete has side effects (e.g., setting deleted_at), using update instead may skip those.
options: Use update(id, { isActive: false }) — returns LeavePolicy | null, no soft-delete side effects
Use softDelete(id) and re-fetch the policy to return LeavePolicy | null — includes any soft-delete side effects

ambiguities.description: GP-002 audit logging: createPolicy, updatePolicy, and deactivatePolicy are state-changing operations. The task does not mention audit logging in the service layer. Should the service emit audit records, or is that deferred to the controller/route layer?
options: Service does not audit — audit is a controller/route concern for this phase
Service must inject IAuditLogRepository and write audit records for create/update/deactivate
